# Project Overview

Creatinine-to-cystatin C discordance and adverse events in patients receiving
platinum-based chemotherapy.

The project repeats the Jiaxuan analysis at **two cohort levels off one
pipeline**: the **entire cohort** (N = 943, all tumour stages) and the
**Local/Early** cohort (N = 322, advanced/metastatic patients excluded). Every
exposure, model, table, figure and download is carried over unchanged at both
levels; both use the Ritu_project creatinine pull and carry the CKD / ESKD
/ AKI variable family ported from the ICI-CKD project.

| | Details |
|---|---|
| **Entire cohort** | no stage filter — N = 943 |
| **Local/Early cohort** | `tumor_stage == "Local/Early"` (stage I–II / local / neoadjuvant) — N = 322 |
| **Excluded from the Local/Early pages** | `tumor_stage == "Advanced/Metastatic"` (stage III–IV) — 621 patients |
| **Primary exposure** | `egfr_diff_pct_per10` — eGFR difference (%) per 10-percentage-point decline |
| **Follow-up** | AKI administratively censored at 365 days; CKD composite to the last creatinine |
| **Modelled outcomes** | AKI within 1 year and the CKD composite only — Fine-Gray competing risks, death at any time as the competing event |
| **Parent project** | [Jiaxuan project](https://tianqi-ouyang.github.io/Cys-C-project-/) |

# Pages and Cohort Sizes

The project runs at two cohort levels off the same pipeline. Both use the
Ritu_project creatinine pull and carry the full CKD / ESKD / AKI variable family.

| Page | Cohort | N |
|---|---|---|
| [**Entire Cohort**](qmd/ritu_entire.qmd) | all platinum, **all stages** | **943** |
| [Whole Cohort](qmd/ritu_whole.qmd) | all platinum, Local/Early only | **322** |
| [Carboplatin Cohort](qmd/ritu_carbo.qmd) | carboplatin, Local/Early | **189** |
| [Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3](qmd/ritu_carbo_auc3.qmd) | carboplatin AUC ≥ 3, Local/Early | **142** |

Entire cohort: 322 Local/Early + 621 Advanced/Metastatic; 596 carboplatin,
347 cisplatin. Within the 322 Local/Early: 189 carboplatin, 133 cisplatin.

**`tumor_stage` differs between the two levels.** It is constant in the
Local/Early cohort, so it is dropped from Table 1 and from every adjuster set
there. In the entire cohort it varies, so it is restored — which makes the
entire-cohort page's model specification the same as the Jiaxuan project's, but
run on the newer creatinine pull and with the kidney variables added. Comparing
the two pages shows what the stage restriction does.

# Exclusion Flow

Inherited from the Jiaxuan pipeline:

1. REDCap records restricted to EMPIs present in `N=596 for tianqi.xlsx` → 946
2. Patients with no matching RPDR lab records excluded (2) → 944
3. Missing baseline cystatin C (`cys_c_baseline` = NA) excluded
4. Missing platinum group (`platin_group` = NA) excluded
5. Record 911 dropped (all RPDR pre-baseline labs fall outside the 45-day window) → **943 = entire cohort**
6. `tumor_stage != "Local/Early"` excluded (621) → **322 = Local/Early cohort**

`ritu_data.qmd` saves after both step 5 (`ritu_full_master.rds`) and step 6
(`ritu_final_master.rds`), so the two cohort levels come from one pipeline run
and are identical in every variable definition.

Details in [Data Management](qmd/ritu_data.qmd).

# What Changed Relative to the Jiaxuan Project

Four kinds of change, nothing else:

**1. Cohort source.** `ritu_data.qmd` applies the stage restriction and writes
`ritu_final_master.rds`; the three analysis pages read that file.

**2. `tumor_stage` dropped as a covariate.** It is constant within this cohort,
so it carries no information and would make the design matrix rank-deficient.
It is removed from Table 1 and from the adjuster set of every Fine-Gray,
cause-specific hazard, Cox PH and linear-subHR model.

**3. Two covariate fixes on the AUC ≥ 3 page only.** That subgroup's filter
empties the `cancer_type_cat_7` "GI" level (0 of 143) and leaves `steroids`
constant at 1 (all 143 received steroids). Together these made the design matrix
rank-deficient — rank 19 of 21 — so `cmprsk::crr` failed for *every* outcome,
including composite grade 2 AEs with 64 events, while the formula interface
silently returned blank coefficient rows. `droplevels()` is re-applied after the
cohort filter and `steroids` is dropped from that page's adjuster sets (it stays
as a descriptive Table 1 row). The whole and carboplatin cohorts are full rank
throughout and keep the original adjuster set.

**4. Sparse-outcome guards.** Several outcomes have very few events in 322
patients (90-day death = 2). Each model helper is wrapped so that a model which
cannot be estimated emits a short note instead of aborting the render. No model
specification is altered.

Unchanged: primary and sensitivity exposures, the `dose_discrep_per25increase`
predictor in the carboplatin pages, reference categories (`sex` = Female,
`ecog_score_cat2` = "0"), the competing-risks framework, eGFR capping rules, and
the Word and PowerPoint downloads. Section numbering changed when the 90-day
outcome models were removed — see `RITU_PROJECT.md` §2.12.

# Power Caveats

Only two outcomes are modelled: **AKI within 1 year** and the **CKD composite**,
both with Fine-Gray competing risks and death at any time as the competing event.
The multivariable models carry roughly 20 covariate degrees of freedom against a
conventional target of 10 events per covariate, so event counts decide what is
readable:

| Cohort | AKI ≤ 1 yr events | CKD composite events | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entire (943) | 198 | 79 | AKI comfortably powered; CKD composite over-parameterised |
| Local/Early (322) | 52 | 30 | both over-parameterised |
| Carboplatin (189) | 24 | 14 | both over-parameterised |
| Carbo AUC ≥ 3 (142) | 12 | 10 | not interpretable |

Univariable columns remain readable throughout. The entire-cohort AKI model is
the only one of the eight that meets the 10-events-per-covariate convention.

# Outcomes

## Grade 2/3 Adverse Events (within 90 days) — derived, not modelled

These are still built by the pipeline and kept in the saved master, but they are
**no longer modelled** on any analysis page. Only AKI within 1 year and the CKD
composite are modelled.

| Outcome | Definition |
|---|---|
| Anemia grade 2 | HGB < 10 g/dL |
| Anemia grade 3 | HGB < 8 g/dL |
| Thrombocytopenia grade 2 | PLT < 75 x10^9/L |
| Thrombocytopenia grade 3 | PLT < 50 x10^9/L |
| AKI grade 2 | Post-baseline CRE > 1.5x pre-baseline CRE (KDIGO) |
| AKI grade 3 | Post-baseline CRE > 3.0x pre-baseline CRE (KDIGO) |
| Composite grade 2 | Any of anemia/thrombocytopenia/AKI grade 2 |
| Composite grade 3 | Any of anemia/thrombocytopenia/AKI grade 3 |

## Hospitalizations & Mortality

Also derived but **no longer modelled**:

- **Hospitalizations:** 11 reason categories; reasons 1–7 define `side_effect` (platinum-related)
- **90-day mortality** (`death_90`): derived from `pt_status` and `days_last_follow_up`
- All outcomes above censored at 90 days

## Long-Horizon Kidney Outcomes (CKD / ESKD / AKI)

Ported from the [ICI-CKD project](https://tianqi-ouyang.github.io/ICI-CKD-/data_management.html),
re-anchored to `baseline_sample_date`. **These are the only outcomes in the
project that are not censored at 90 days** — a qualifying CKD episode must be
*sustained for ≥ 90 days*, so they use the full length of RPDR creatinine
follow-up (median 445 days, max 1167).

| Outcome | Definition | Entire 943 | Local/Early 322 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aki` | **Within 1 year**: CRE > 1.5 × median of prior 90 d, **or** ≥ 0.3 mg/dL above the prior-2-day low | 197 (20.9 %) | 51 (15.8 %) |
| `aki_any` | Same rule, no time limit (reference only, not modelled) | 240 (25.5 %) | 63 (19.6 %) |
| `ckd_incidence` | Sustained ≥ 90 d: `pct_drop > 0.25` & eGFR < 60 & baseline ≥ 60 | 61 (6.5 %) | 21 (6.5 %) |
| `ckd_incidence_any` | Sustained ≥ 90 d: baseline ≥ 60 → eGFR < 60, **no % requirement** | 89 (9.4 %) | 37 (11.5 %) |
| `ckd_progression` | Sustained ≥ 90 d: baseline **< 60** *and* a further `pct_drop > 0.30` | 8 (0.8 %) | 5 (1.6 %) |
| `eskd_defination_1` | Sustained ≥ 90 d: eGFR < 10 | 1 (0.1 %) | 1 (0.3 %) |
| `esrd_kt_after_ici` | ESRD / KT / dialysis ICD code after baseline | 2 (0.2 %) | 1 (0.3 %) |
| `eskd_composite` | `esrd_kt_after_ici == 1 \| eskd_defination_1 == 1` | 2 (0.2 %) | 1 (0.3 %) |
| `ckd_composite` | `eskd_composite \| ckd_incidence \| ckd_progression` | 70 (7.4 %) | 26 (8.1 %) |

`ckd_composite` uses `ckd_incidence` (> 25 %), not `ckd_incidence_any`. The
progression definition now requires a further > 30 % drop; previously it counted
anyone below 60 before and after, i.e. stable CKD, which is why that count fell
from 61 to 8.

## Delta eGFR vs Baseline at 90 / 180 / 365 Days

Change in creatinine eGFR from `eGFR_CRE_baseline`, using the creatinine
**closest to each mark** and only when it falls within **± 45 days** of it. Days
run from `baseline_sample_date`. Built in Section 5.16b of
[Data Management](qmd/ritu_data.qmd) and reported per cohort in §2.3 (whole,
entire) and §3.3 (carboplatin pages). Descriptive only — not modelled.

**Negative means decline**, i.e. eGFR at the mark minus eGFR at baseline. This is
the opposite sign to `pct_drop` in the pipeline.

| Mark | n (of 943) | Δ eGFR, median [IQR] | Δ eGFR %, median [IQR] |
|---|---|---|---|
| Day 90 | 876 (92.9 %) | 1.0 [−6.2, 7.7] | 1.1 [−7.5, 9.8] |
| Day 180 | 710 (75.3 %) | −2.6 [−11.9, 4.2] | −2.8 [−14.5, 5.7] |
| Day 365 | 517 (54.8 %) | −6.2 [−15.3, 1.6] | −7.6 [−18.5, 1.5] |

Local/Early (322): day 90 n = 301, Δ 0.9 [−5.9, 7.2]; day 180 n = 244,
Δ −2.2 [−12.7, 3.4]; day 365 n = 186, Δ −7.1 [−15.3, −0.5].

The two carboplatin cohorts decline less: carboplatin (189) Δ +2.1 at day 90 and
−4.2 at day 365; AUC ≥ 3 (142) Δ +2.1 and −6.0.

Two things to read with it. The **realized day is tight** — median 86, 179 and 364
against nominal 90, 180 and 365 — so the window is doing its job rather than
quietly shifting the timepoint. But **coverage falls with time**, from 93 % at day
90 to 55 % at day 365, because creatinine is drawn less often once treatment
ends. The day-365 figures therefore describe the half of the cohort still being
monitored a year out, who are not a random half.

The ± 45-day window matches the pipeline's existing baseline-lab window
(`pre_CRE_45days`) and is the widest that keeps the 90- and 180-day marks from
drawing on the same measurement. Without any window every patient gets a value
at every mark, but the closest creatinine to day 365 would be over 276 days away
for a tenth of the cohort.

## Competing-Risk Models (death competing)

Fine-Gray models for `egfr_diff_pct_per10` are in §4.12–4.13 of the whole and
entire pages and §5.12–5.13 of the carboplatin pages. These are the only two
long-horizon outcomes modelled; the 90-day adverse-event and hospitalization
outcomes are modelled with the 90-day competing event in §4 / §5.

The competing event is **death at any time**, `death_days_any` — `death_90` is
capped at 90 days and cannot place a death in time beyond day 90, so it cannot
serve over a multi-year horizon. `death_days_any` is the **union of the two
sources** that carry a death date: the RPDR `Date_Of_Death` when there is one,
otherwise the REDCap last-follow-up date for a patient whose `pt_status` is
"Dead". The two do not nest — 22 REDCap deaths have no RPDR date, and RPDR dates
deaths REDCap has not caught up with — so the union gives 300 dated deaths in
the entire cohort against 278 from RPDR alone, and 37 against 34 in
Local/Early. Someone flagged deceased in RPDR with no date who is still alive in
REDCap stays censored. Censoring is at the last creatinine.

| Model | Entire 943 | Local/Early 322 | Carbo 189 | AUC ≥ 3 142 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AKI ≤ 1 yr | subHR 1.30 (1.16, 1.45), p < 0.001 | 1.11 (0.86, 1.44), p = 0.43 | 1.13 (0.82, 1.56), p = 0.45 | 1.23 (0.66, 2.32), p = 0.51 |
| CKD composite, any time | 1.16 (1.03, 1.31), p = 0.018 | 1.52 (1.14, 2.02), p = 0.004 | 1.82 (0.98, 3.39), p = 0.059 | 1.73 (0.69, 4.34), p = 0.25 |

Each outcome is now run **three ways** — same competing event, same non-kidney
adjusters, differing only in the kidney adjuster or the exposure:

| | Exposure | Kidney adjuster | § whole / entire | § carboplatin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original | (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys − Cockcroft-Gault) / CG | `cockcroft` | 4 | 5 |
| Variant 1 | the same | CKD-EPI Cr-Cys | 5 | 6 |
| Variant 2 | (CKD-EPI CysC − CKD-EPI Cr) / Cr | `cockcroft` | 6 | 7 |

Both exposures read per 10 percentage-point decline. `RITU_PROJECT.md` §2.14 has
all twenty-four estimates, and explains why **variant 1 is not a sensitivity
check of the original**: the exposure is a ratio of CKD-EPI Cr-Cys to
Cockcroft-Gault, so the two models condition on different halves of it and
answer different questions.

Events / competing deaths: AKI **198 + 115** (entire), 52 + 8 (Local/Early);
CKD composite **79 + 282** (entire), 30 + 34 (Local/Early). Only the
entire-cohort AKI model is comfortably powered against ~21 covariates.

All of the above are **Table 1 rows** on all three analysis pages, together with
`esrd_kt` (ESRD / KT at or before baseline, n = 1), `eGFR_CRE_baseline`,
`ckd_stage_baseline` and `last_cre_days`. They also keep a dedicated section —
2.2 on the whole-cohort page, 3.2 on the carboplatin pages — carrying the median
time to each event, the length of creatinine follow-up, and the `aki` vs
`AKI_kdigo_90days` cross-tabulation that Table 1 cannot show.

AKI and the CKD composite are now **modelled** with Fine-Gray competing risks
(see below). The remaining kidney variables stay descriptive.

`aki` is a different variable from the existing `AKI_g2_90days` /
`AKI_kdigo_90days`: it compares each creatinine against the patient's own
preceding 90-day median across the whole record, not against a fixed
pre-baseline value inside 90 days. In the whole cohort they agree on 19
patients, `aki` alone flags 44, and `AKI_kdigo_90days` alone flags 14.

# Data Sources

| Source | Used for |
|---|---|
| REDCap export `CystatinCInPatientsO_DATA_2026-10-09_1107.csv` (refreshed follow-up) | Baseline, treatment, outcomes |
| RPDR **Ritu_project** (`mes98_1008261634…`, Oct 2026) | **All creatinine** — 50,046 rows — and `Vital_status` / `Date_Of_Death` |
| RPDR **2026-03-19** (`mes98_0318261449…`) | HGB, PLT, ALB, GHBA1C (128,156 rows), plus all diagnoses and medications |

The REDCap export was refreshed on 2026-10-09 with updated follow-up: median
follow-up rose from 378 to 539 days, recorded deaths from 207 to 272, and one
patient was reclassified Local/Early → Advanced/Metastatic (so the Local/Early
cohort is 322, not 323). That export also carries `name`, `mgh_mrn` and `dob`
columns, which are dropped at read time and never enter the dataset or this site.

The Ritu_project RPDR pull is a creatinine-only extract — it has no `Dia` or
`Med` file and no HGB/PLT/ALB/GHBA1C — so it supplies creatinine plus vital
status, and the 2026-03-19 pull supplies everything else. Both cover the same
973 EMPIs.

It replaced an earlier creatinine pull in October 2026 and is a strict extension
of it: 50,046 creatinine values against 48,843, with follow-up running to
2026-08-30 instead of 2026-06-28 and no changed values. Its `Dem` file is also
newer — 288 dated deaths against 262, latest 2026-10-06 — and those 26 extra
dates are additions, not corrections. The extra follow-up is what the
longitudinal eGFR, CKD and AKI outcomes are built from, and it added 9 CKD
composite events in the entire cohort (70 → 79) and 28 more patients with a
day-365 eGFR.

# Key Variables

## Exposure

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `egfr_diff_pct` | 100 × (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed − Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault |
| `egfr_diff_pct_per10` | Primary reporting scale: per 10-percentage-point **decline** |
| `egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10` | Sensitivity: CKD-EPI 2012 CysC vs CKD-EPI 2021 Cr, per 10 % decline |
| `dose_discrep_per25increase` | Carboplatin dose discrepancy (actual − predicted mg) / 25 |

## eGFR & Kidney Function

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `baseline_cre_egfr` | CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine eGFR (mL/min/1.73m²) |
| `ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys` | CKD-EPI 2012 combined creatinine + cystatin C eGFR (mL/min/1.73m²) |
| `ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex` | Combined CKD-EPI eGFR adjusted for BSA (mL/min) |
| `cockcroft` | Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance |
| `ckd_stage_cre` | KDIGO G-stage from `baseline_cre_egfr` (G3a / G3b kept apart) |
| `ckd_stage_cre_cys` | KDIGO G-stage from `ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys` (G3a / G3b kept apart) |
| `eGFR_CRE_baseline` | CKD-EPI creatinine eGFR at `pre_CRE_45days` — the baseline the CKD outcomes are referenced to |
| `ckd_stage_baseline` | KDIGO stage from `eGFR_CRE_baseline`, ICI-CKD convention (G3a + G3b collapsed into one stage 3) |
| `eGFR_CRE_d90` / `_d180` / `_d365` | Creatinine eGFR from the creatinine closest to that day, within ± 45 days of it |
| `cre_day_d90` / `_d180` / `_d365` | The actual day of the creatinine used — lets the gap from the nominal mark be checked |
| `delta_egfr_d90` / `_d180` / `_d365` | eGFR at the mark − `eGFR_CRE_baseline`, mL/min/1.73m². **Negative = decline** |
| `delta_egfr_pct_d90` / `_d180` / `_d365` | The same change as a percentage of baseline. **Negative = decline** |

Only `ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex` is capped at 125 mL/min; the indexed value
and `cockcroft` are uncapped. Uncapped values feed the eGFR difference; capped
values feed the dose-discrepancy calculation.

Both CKD stage variables use the standard KDIGO G categories — G1 ≥ 90,
G2 60–89, G3a 45–59, G3b 30–44, G4 15–29, G5 < 15 mL/min/1.73m² — and are built
from the **BSA-indexed** eGFRs, the scale KDIGO staging is defined on. No patient
in this cohort reaches G5, so that level is dropped rather than shown as an empty
Table 1 row. They are descriptive Table 1 rows only; no model adjusts for them
(the continuous eGFRs already appear in the adjuster sets).

## Competing Risk Variables

| Pattern | Description |
|---|---|
| `cmp_time_<outcome>` | Time for the competing-risk model |
| `cmp_status_<outcome>` | 0 = censored, 1 = event, 2 = death |
| `death_days_any` / `death_any` | Days to death at any time — union of RPDR `Date_Of_Death` and the REDCap last-follow-up date when `pt_status` is "Dead". The competing event for §4.12–4.13 / §5.12–5.13 |

# Reproducing

```bash
cd "/Users/to909/Desktop/Meg/Cystain C redcap/Ritu project" && quarto render
```

`ritu_data.qmd` renders first and produces the `ritu_final_master.rds` that the
three analysis pages read. Full project notes are in `RITU_PROJECT.md`.
